profile.campus: San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas (QTS San Antonio 2 campus)
profile.address: Per QTS's own site: 8535 Potranco Road, San Antonio, TX 78251. This registry's OSM based address tag for the facility records 8635 Potranco Road, an unresolved one digit discrepancy not checked against a Bexar County parcel record in this research.
profile.reading:
QTS San Antonio 2 is a wholesale and colocation data center campus on Potranco Road on the west side of San Antonio, Texas, in Bexar County, roughly twenty minutes from San Antonio International Airport by the operator's own description. QTS's own site places the facility at 8535 Potranco Road, San Antonio, TX 78251, on a 32 acre campus with more than 90 megawatts of power capacity available to the site. That power figure is presented by QTS only as a general campus capacity number, without QTS specifying whether it describes utility feed capacity, installed IT load, or some combination, so it is treated here as an operator stated campus capacity rather than assigned to any one of this registry's four power categories. This registry's own address tag for the facility records 8635 Potranco Road, a hundred numbers off from QTS's own published address, a discrepancy that could not be resolved against a Bexar County parcel record in this research and is noted rather than silently resolved one way or the other. No square footage, building count, data hall count, tier rating, or year built figure for San Antonio 2 is published on QTS's own site, and none was found in trade press or public filings during this research.

QTS, formally Quality Technology Services, was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, by Chad Williams, and grew through a combination of acquisitions and ground up construction into a national wholesale and colocation platform before going public as a real estate investment trust in 2013. That public period ended in 2021, when Blackstone's non traded real estate income trust completed an approximately 10 billion dollar acquisition of QTS on August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own announcement, taking the company private again. QTS describes its business model as hyperscale neutral, meaning it leases built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own retail cloud service, a model it shares with peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne. Since the Blackstone acquisition, QTS has continued to expand rather than slow down, including a large campus buildout in Glendale, Arizona and continued development in the Dallas Fort Worth area, evidence of sustained capital investment across its portfolio under private ownership. QTS operates a wider national footprint beyond San Antonio, including other Texas metros, Arizona, Ohio, New Jersey, Illinois, and Colorado, per QTS's own site, though this research did not attempt to verify a precise company wide facility count.

San Antonio's data center sector, of which this campus is part, sits on a grid served by CPS Energy, the city owned electric and gas utility. Local reporting by the nonprofit newsroom San Antonio Report has described CPS Energy as serving twenty one data centers citywide as of early 2026, generating on the order of 110 million dollars in annual revenue from that customer class, with fifty nine additional data center projects reported in various stages of planning, and Bexar County overall described as home to at least thirty data centers. CPS Energy has published a formal large load interconnection process for customers seeking major new electric capacity, and the grid operator ERCOT commissioned an independent technical review of CPS Energy's large load additions project in 2025, evidence that utility capacity planning for data center growth in this market, of which QTS San Antonio 2 is one customer among many, is an active and closely watched subject rather than a settled one. No Bexar County Commissioners Court tax abatement agreement, City of San Antonio Chapter 380 economic development grant, or contested zoning hearing naming QTS San Antonio 2 specifically was found in this research, an open gap rather than an assumption that no such agreement exists.

reading.body:
QTS San Antonio 2 is a 32 acre wholesale and colocation campus on the west side of San Antonio operated by Quality Technology Services, a privately held subsidiary of Blackstone acquired in 2021. The operator publishes 90 megawatts or more of power capacity available across the campus without specifying whether that figure represents utility feed, installed IT load, or standby generation, so it is treated here as a general operator stated capacity rather than assigned to any specific power category. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 90 megawatts of IT load would be roughly 2,250 racks, though the operator does not disclose what portion of the published 90 megawatts is available for live compute load versus utility feed or standby capacity.

No building count, square footage, data hall count, tier rating, or year built is published for this campus. QTS does not disclose which tenants occupy San Antonio 2 or what workloads they run. The campus sits on CPS Energy's grid, which serves at least 21 operating data centers citywide as of early 2026 and has 59 additional projects in planning, meaning utility capacity for new load is an active planning subject rather than a settled one.

San Antonio 2 would rank outside the top 19 data center campuses in Texas by published megawatt capacity, placing it among the 114 mapped facilities in the state that do not disclose power figures. The state's 19 published facilities account for 475 megawatts total, so the 90 megawatts stated for this campus, if it were disclosed with the same specificity as leading facilities, would place it in the middle tier of the Texas portfolio by capacity alone.
